title: Rural area LPG booking period reduced from 45 to 25 days
content:
NEW DELHI: With improvement in LPG supplies and a fall in refill backlogs, govt Monday reduced the minimum time gap for booking LPG refills in rural areas to 25 days from 45 days, bringing it on a par with the interval for urban consumers, reports Atul Mathur. Union minister of state for petroleum and natural gas Suresh Gopi said the restriction had been imposed amid pressure on LPG supplies following the outbreak of the conflict in West Asia, with the booking interval set at 25 days in urban areas and 45 days in rural areas. "However, in view of the current LPG supply situation improving and the significant reduction in refill backlog, Centre has relaxed this restriction. Now, all domestic LPG consumers, regardless of urban or rural, can book refills at an interval of 25 days," Gopi said. Petroleum ministry has issued an order to oil marketing companies IOC, BPCL and HPCL, asking them to implement this with immediate effect.

title: SC rejects panel's plea for 6 more months to define Aravali hills & ranges
content:
NEW DELHI: "Why don't you simply say that the matter be heard after my retirement," asked an exasperated CJI Surya Kant as a bench led by him outrightly declined a request from the high-powered committee for six more months' time to draft a comprehensive definition of Aravali hills and ranges to protect the eco-sensitive area from mining and various commercial activities and fixed a Nov 30 deadline for submission of the final report. Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for HPC, told a bench of CJI, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that HPC would need six more months to file a detailed report, which would include completing public hearings and considering views of stakeholders. CJI Kant is to retire on Feb 9. A bench led by him had stayed the operation of SC's Nov 20 judgement accepting a very liberal definition of Aravali that had caused an uproar among environmentalists.

Detained Pak national repatriated via intl border

JAMMU: A Pakistani man detained near the international border in Jammu’s Kanachak sector last week was repatriated on Monday. Troops of BSF’s 44Bn caught the intruder on Sept 3 near a forward area border outpost. During questioning, he identified himself as Nazir Sadhir from Luni Pundra village in Sialkot and allegedly told investigators that he had inadvertently crossed into Indian territory, officials said. Security agencies investigated his claims, following which BSF officials contacted their Pakistani counterparts and initiated the repatriation process. On Monday, Sadhir was handed over to Pakistan Rangers at Golpattan border outpost along the international border after a flag meeting, officials said.

End of Article

title: Balance needed between scientific probe and right to privacy, says SC
content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday said technological advancements have made criminal investigation far more complicated and a challenge for the investigating agencies, as they get the stick from the court and the victim for not conducting the probe scientifically, and on the other hand, are accused of violation of privacy if they do. “A balance needs to be struck,” said a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, while dealing with an application by journalist Abhishek Upadhyay, who claimed to be whistleblower on pilferage of Ram temple donations, and has accused Ghaziabad police of making an FIR in an alleged road rage case the pretext for seeking his digital footprints from June 1 from social media platforms to find his sources.

End of Article
